name: MuffinEMU (TrollStore)
subtitle: Wii U emulation for iPhone and iPad - TrollStore build.
description: The install source for MuffinEMU, a Wii U emulator for iPhone and iPad built on Cemu. This source serves the ad-hoc signed build for TrollStore and jailbroken devices, with the JIT entitlements embedded so the recompiler can get executable memory. On SideStore or AltStore use the standard source instead - those re-sign at install and would strip these entitlements.

apps.subtitle: Wii U emulator - TrollStore build
apps.localizedDescription:
MuffinEMU is a Wii U emulator for iPhone and iPad, iOS 15 and later, built on Cemu: PowerPC interpreters, an AArch64 recompiler, Cafe OS HLE and a native Metal renderer under a SwiftUI app with a measured Wii U GamePad layout. Some MeloCafe cores and bug fixes have been brought over to MuffinEMU.

This source serves the ad-hoc signed build for TrollStore and jailbroken devices, with the JIT entitlements embedded so the recompiler can get executable memory. On SideStore or AltStore use the standard source instead - those re-sign at install and would strip these entitlements.

Bring your own games and keys. No copyrighted content is distributed here.

MuffinEMU, Wii U emulation for iPhone and iPad, built from commit 23102e1f8f5ad2c640de4cf334460d0b34b8c684.

**`MuffinEMU.ipa`** - SideStore / AltStore / LiveContainer. Unsigned; they re-sign
with your own Apple ID at install.

**`MuffinEMU-fakesigned.ipa`** - TrollStore or jailbroken only, with the JIT
entitlements embedded.

The recompiler needs a JIT enabler (StikJIT, SideStore, LiveContainer) and the
"Use the recompiler (JIT)" switch in Settings; without both it runs the
interpreter. `MuffinEMU.app.dSYM.zip` is only needed to symbolicate a crash report.

MuffinEMU is built on Cemu. Some MeloCafe cores and bug fixes have been brought over to MuffinEMU.

## Fixed (for real this time): Single Screen rendering tiny in the top-left corner

This took three attempts across v2.4-v2.6 to actually nail down, so here's the
honest account rather than just "fixed": the emulated screen was rendering small
and pinned to the top-left instead of fullscreen. v2.4's fix (a GeometryReader
wrapped around the render view) made it worse, not better - a GeometryReader
reports close to zero size until its parent already has one, and the surrounding
stack was sizing itself to that near-zero content. The real fix checks the actual
original Muffin app's own shipped single-screen code, which never needed any of
this: with only one screen to show, it's mounted directly with no computed frame
at all, because there's no second screen to share space with. Single Screen mode

## Fixed: Single Screen / Adaptive rendering tiny in the top-left corner

v2.3's Screen Layout port left the emulated screen rendering small, pinned to the
top-left corner, instead of fullscreen - present from the very first launch, not
just after swapping. Root cause: the view showing the TV/GamePad screen is a raw
UIKit view wrapped for SwiftUI, and `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)`
doesn't reliably force a view like that to actually fill the space SwiftUI gives it,
unlike a native SwiftUI view. MeloCafe's own equivalent avoids this by wrapping its
view in an inner `GeometryReader` and applying an explicit, measured size instead of
a flexible one - that wrapper was missing here and is now in place. The emulated
screen fills the same space the on-screen GamePad buttons already span.

## Screen Layout - a real port this time

Single Screen, Adaptive (Both Screens) and GamePad-top-right are now a true port of
MeloCafe's own screen-composition logic, not a hand-rewritten equivalent - same
`ScreenLayout` model, same view behavior. An earlier attempt at this broke things
(screens going black when swapping between TV/GamePad); the actual cause was traced
to MuffinEMU's render containers being recreated on every remount instead of staying
stable, and fixed at that root instead of worked around. The in-game swap button and
external-display routing are unchanged.

## What's new since v1.6

- **Save states (new)** - freeze and restore a running game, 4 numbered slots per
  game, reachable from a bookmark button in the top bar while a title is running.
  Persistent: stored under the app's own Documents folder, survives relaunching the
  app. Real scope, stated plainly rather than oversold:
  - This captures the game's memory, not a full snapshot. It does NOT save GPU/renderer
    state (textures, shaders, in-flight command buffers) - those are caches the game
    rebuilds from memory as it runs, so right after loading a texture or effect that
    changed since the save might flash its old look for a moment. That's a visual
    glitch, not lost data, and it clears itself on the next frame.

## What's fixed in this build

- **The whole app freezing when you hit pause** - pausing suspends every guest CPU
  thread under the core's own scheduler lock, and that call was running synchronously
  on the main thread (both from the pause button and from the auto-pause-on-background
  handler). If a guest thread holding that lock was itself waiting on something that
  only resolves once the main thread's run loop is free - a Metal command buffer
  completion handler dispatched back to the main queue is exactly this shape - the main
  thread and the guest thread wait on each other forever: not a slow pause, the whole
  app stops responding to anything, pause button included. Both call sites now run on a
